vector3.blur.radius_tip: Blur radius in pixels of a 1080p frame; it scales with the resolution.
vector3.blur.clear_tip: Radius of a sharp area in the middle of the screen. 0 blurs the whole frame.
vector3.vfx.remove_effect: Remove this effect from the keyframe
vector3.rays.note: Overworld only: the sun by day, the moon by night (cool light, stronger at full moon). It must be on or near the screen; blocks and leaves cut the sky into shafts.
vector3.rays.length_tip: How far the rays reach towards the sun, as a share of the distance to it.
vector3.rays.decay_tip: How quickly light fades along a ray. Lower values give shorter, softer shafts.
vector3.rays.falloff_tip: How strongly the rays fade away from the sun. 0 keeps them even across the screen.
vector3.rays.sky_tip: Open sky, including the sun, is a light source. Everything else blocks it.
vector3.rays.bright_tip: Very bright things (glowing blocks, sunlit clouds) also send out rays.
vector3.ao.limit: Uses visible depth; hidden geometry cannot occlude.
vector3.ssr.limit: Only visible screen pixels can appear in reflections.
vector3.grade.curve_hint: Drag points; double-click to add; right-click an inner point to remove.
vector3.bloom.dirt_tip: Resource ID (namespace:path.png) or an image file on disk.
vector3.history.title: History
vector3.track.title: Tracks
vector3.blast.truncated: The region is too large: only the first 32768 blocks fly.
vector3.blast.trajectory.label: Trajectory
vector3.blast.path_hint: Points are in the shape's local space; drag them in the viewport with M. The path runs from the path start through the points to the scatter center.
vector3.blast.scatter_center.tooltip: In the shape's local space; drag it in the viewport with M.
vector3.blast.flatten.tooltip: Squashes the scatter cloud vertically; 0 lays the blocks out flat.
vector3.blast.stagger.tooltip: How much of the progress is spent starting the pieces one after another.
vector3.blast.order.label: Order
vector3.blast.from_origin_hint: Pieces fly between the scatter center and the shape; the nearer a block is to the origin, the earlier it breaks away (or settles, when gathering).
vector3.blast.sweep_hint: A volume moves from the sweep start to the sweep end during the stagger part of the progress; what it touches breaks away (or settles, when gathering). Blocks it never touches stay put.
vector3.blast.origin.tooltip: Where the blast starts: those blocks leave first when dispersing and settle first when gathering. The explosion also bulges out from here.
vector3.blast.easing.label: Easing
vector3.blast.clump.tooltip: In blocks. From a larger start to a smaller end, the clumps break up level by level (16, 8, 4, 2, 1) as they fly.
vector3.blast.clump_jitter.tooltip: How far the clump borders wander from a regular grid. Clumps still nest, so each one breaks only into pieces of itself.
vector3.blast.start_end_hint: Pairs are start, end: assembled, then scattered.
vector3.particle.lifetime.tooltip: Random between the two values. 0 keeps the particle type's own lifetime.
vector3.particle.tint.tooltip: Tints each particle with the Color above. Off keeps the particle type's own colors.
vector3.particle.native_motion.tooltip: Let the particle type randomize the start velocity as vanilla does, instead of using exactly the shape's direction and speed.
vector3.particle.local_space.tooltip: Live particles move along with the emitter.
vector3.particle.rate_over_distance.tool: Extra particles for every block the emitter moves, for trails.
vector3.particle.burst.tooltip: Particles emitted at once at each burst. 0 turns bursts off.
vector3.particle.thickness.tooltip: 0 emits from the surface only, 1 from the whole volume.
vector3.particle.direction_hint: Rotate the shape (R) to aim it; the cone, box and edge emit along its local +Y.
vector3.particle.force.tooltip: A constant acceleration in world space, such as wind or buoyancy.
vector3.particle.noise.tooltip: Random jitter added to the velocity every tick.
vector3.particle.color_over_lifetime.too: Blends from the start color to the end color as the particle ages.
vector3.particle.end_size.tooltip: Size multiplier at the end of the lifetime; 1 keeps the size.
vector3.particle.override_physics.toolti: Replace the particle type's gravity, drag and collision.
vector3.particle.drag.tooltip: Share of the velocity lost per second.
vector3.keyframe.obj_pivots.tooltip: Where each part turns for Entity Pose keyframes. Defaults to the centre of the part's faces.
vector3.keyframe.obj_lighting.tooltip: Shades faces by the way they point, like vanilla lights entities, so the model keeps its form without a shader pack. With a shader pack, the pack lights it instead.
vector3.keyframe.name: Name
vector3.keyframe.layer.screen.tooltip:
Draw the shape flat on the screen with an orthographic projection, above the world and below the fade.
Coordinates are 1080p reference pixels: (0, 0) is the screen center, y points up, the screen is always 1080 tall; larger z is in front.
Not affected by shader packs; entity mounting and billboarding are off on this layer.
vector3.keyframe.entity_source.world.too: Draws an entity already in the replay, as it moves and animates, at this shape's position, rotation and scale.
vector3.keyframe.entity_pose_hint: To pose it, add an Entity Pose keyframe and pick this shape as its entity.
vector3.keyframe.bypass_shaders.tooltip: With a shader pack active: draw this unshaded together with the other shapes, so it occludes and is occluded by them correctly. Off: the shader pack shades it like the world.
vector3.keyframe_type.name: Shape
vector3.shape_manager.title: Shape Manager
vector3.shape_manager.copy_hint: Drag onto a shape to parent it, right-click to edit, middle-click to copy ID
vector3.look_to.ends_scope.tooltip: From a keyframe until the next one, the camera looks at the target, moving toward the next keyframe's target. A keyframe marked End Scope stops it and only provides that final target.
vector3.skip.ends_scope.tooltip: Playback and export jump from a start keyframe straight to the next End Skip keyframe. Scrubbing while paused still shows the skipped part.
vector3.prefab.drag_hint: Drag onto the timeline, or double-click to place at the cursor.
vector3.prefab.name: Name
vector3.prefab.skipped_block_overrides: Block Override keyframes can't be saved in a prefab and were left out.
vector3.dolly_zoom.ends_scope.tooltip: From a keyframe until the next one, the camera follows the target, blending distance, framing and direction toward the next keyframe. A keyframe marked End Scope stops it.
vector3.dolly_zoom.frame_height.tooltip: How many blocks tall the view is at the target's distance. Keep it the same between keyframes for a dolly zoom: the target keeps its size while the background stretches.
vector3.shape_manager.instant_preview.to: Apply keyframes live while dragging them on the timeline, instead of only on release
vector3.keyframe.glow_sdf_only: Glow only works with custom (.ttf/.otf) fonts
vector3.gizmo.place_hint: Middle click: move to the block/entity under the cursor (Ctrl: snap to the block cell)
vector3.shape_manager.drop_to_unparent: Drop here to remove its parent
vector3.eyedropper.entity_tooltip: Pick an entity in the viewport
vector3.eyedropper.shape_tooltip: Pick a shape in the viewport
vector3.eyedropper.hint: Click a target in the viewport (right click / Esc to cancel)
vector3.shape_manager.auto_key.tooltip: Picking a shape with nothing selected edits it at the playhead; moving it creates a keyframe there

vector3.motion_path.title: Motion Paths
vector3.properties.empty: Select a keyframe on the timeline to edit it here.
vector3.curve.multi: Editing the speed curve of %s keyframes together
vector3.curve.hint: Shapes the time from this keyframe to the next. Drag points and handles (Alt: break handle, Ctrl: snap), double-click to add, right-click to remove.
vector3.multi.locked: Values differ. Hold Ctrl to unlock and set them all.
vector3.properties.clipboard_hint: %s rows selected · %s on clipboard · Ctrl+right-click to select, Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V
vector3.clips.title: Clips
vector3.clips.drag_hint: Drag a replay onto the timeline to add it as a clip. Order clips by dragging them on the Clips track, then apply.
vector3.clips.range_hint: Source ticks, 0 to %s. Apply to take effect.
vector3.clips.incompatible_detail: It was recorded on %s, this project on %s.
vector3.clips.composing_hint: You can keep editing; the replay reopens once the clips are composed.
vector3.loop.ends_scope.tooltip: Playback and export jump from here back to the previous Loop keyframe until its repeats are used up.
vector3.loop.count.tooltip: How many extra times the section plays. 1 plays it twice. Pausing the replay resets the count.
vector3.fade.opacity.tooltip: 0 shows the scene, 1 covers it completely. Keyframes blend between each other; use two keyframes for a fade in or out.
vector3.repeat.tooltip: Repeats this track's keyframes after its last one.
vector3.ripple.nothing: Ripple delete: no time to close
vector3.ripple.overlap: Ripple delete: keyframes would land on each other
vector3.camera_preview.title: Camera Preview
vector3.camera_preview.iris: The camera preview is off while a shader pack is in use. Tick the box above to try it anyway.
vector3.camera_preview.no_camera: No camera keyframes at the playhead.

vector3.help.title: Help
vector3.camera_preview.with_shaders.tool: Renders the world twice per frame through the shader pack. It costs about double, and effects that reuse the previous frame (TAA, motion blur, auto exposure) may smear or flicker between the two views.
vector3.camera_preview.detach: Main view doesn't follow the camera
vector3.camera_preview.detach.tooltip: While this window is open, camera keyframes (position, FOV, shake, Look To, Dolly Zoom) only drive the preview, so the main view stays where you put it during playback. Exports are unaffected.
vector3.keyframe.obj_mode.mtl.tooltip: Uses the .mtl files the OBJ names (mtllib / usemtl): each material's colour (Kd), opacity (d) and texture (map_Kd), found next to the OBJ. Colour still tints the whole model.
vector3.entity_pose.mode.tooltip: Replace: switched-on rotations hold exactly these values; offsets are from the part's rest position. Add: rotation and offset go on top of what the part already has. Several tracks can pose one entity: they apply in track order, each on top of the one above, and channels left off keep what they had.
vector3.entity_pose.capture.tooltip: Copies the entity's pose as it is animated right now into this keyframe, for every part.
vector3.entity_pose.not_loaded: The entity isn't loaded at the playhead.
vector3.entity_pose.no_parts: Pick a loaded entity to list its model parts.
vector3.entity_pose.part.head: Head
vector3.entity_pose.gizmo_part: Edit this part with the viewport gizmo (or right-click its marker there)
vector3.entity_pose.rotate.tooltip: Drive this part's rotation from this track. Leave it off to let another track (or the animation) drive it.
vector3.entity_pose.move.tooltip: Drive this part's offset from this track. Leave it off to let another track (or the animation) drive it.
vector3.distribute.too_few: Distribute: select keyframes on at least two ticks
vector3.distribute.too_short: Distribute: not enough ticks for every keyframe
vector3.distribute.overlap: Distribute: keyframes would land on unselected ones
vector3.packet_compat.tooltip: Keep replaying past what Flashback can't read: packets it can't replay (e.g. minecraft:transfer), actions that fail, or data recorded in a format this version reads differently. Each kind of problem is logged once.
vector3.channels.track.tooltip: Each keyframe on this track can key only some properties. Each property then blends between the keyframes that key it, and holds its nearest one outside them.
vector3.channels.keyed.tooltip: Properties this keyframe keys. Editing a property keys it.
vector3.channels.selected.tooltip: Whether the selected keyframe keys this property
vector3.channels.key_here.tooltip: Key only this property at the playhead (a new keyframe holding what is shown now)
vector3.channels.toggle_here.tooltip: Key or unkey this property on the keyframe at the playhead
vector3.channels.cannot_key: This keyframe type can't be keyed from its current value; add a keyframe instead
vector3.channels.all.tooltip: Make the selected keyframe key every property again
vector3.mount.model_part.unavailable: The entity isn't loaded, or has no posable model
vector3.mount.model_part.tooltip: Attach to this part of the entity's model (e.g. a hand or the head), following its animation and pose keyframes.
vector3.track_entity.follow_part_rotatio: The camera turns with the model part in yaw, pitch and roll. The yaw / pitch offsets and roll then count from the part's own facing, and the view offset turns with it.
vector3.vfx.focus_tip: Distance from the camera to the focus plane, in blocks.
vector3.vfx.focus_range_tip: Depth around the focus plane that stays fully sharp, in blocks.
vector3.vfx.focus_overlay_tip: While this keyframe is selected, tints the sharp zone and draws a line where the focus plane cuts the scene. With the camera preview detached, the plane is drawn in the world in front of the shot camera instead.
vector3.vfx.dof_strength_tip: Largest blur radius, as a share of the screen height.
vector3.vfx.blur_distance_tip: Distance in blocks at which the blur is well developed.
vector3.dof.autofocus_tip: Focus on whatever is at the centre of the screen.
vector3.dof.autofocus_smoothing_tip: Half-life of the focus change, in seconds: how long autofocus takes to cover half the way to a new subject.
vector3.dof.aperture_tip: How quickly the blur grows away from the focus plane. Higher values give a shallower depth of field.
vector3.dof.samples_tip: Samples per ring, times ten. Higher is smoother and slower.
vector3.dof.chromatic_tip: Splits the colours in blurred areas, more towards the screen edges.
vector3.dof.anamorphic_tip: Stretches the blur vertically, like an anamorphic lens.
vector3.dof.fov_scaled_tip: Blur grows as the field of view narrows, like zooming in with a real lens.
vector3.dof.tilt_tip: Tilts the focus plane across the screen, for a tilt-shift look.
vector3.vfx.lut_tip: Resource ID or image file of a 256 x 16 LUT: sixteen 16 x 16 blue slices arranged horizontally.
vector3.expression.copy_reference.toolti: Copies an expression that reads this parameter from another track's expression, e.g. Cube.position.y
vector3.expression.enabled.tooltip: Enabled: when off, the keyframed value is used
vector3.expression.missing: This parameter isn't shown for the current settings, so the expression does nothing right now
vector3.expression.help:
Expression. time (seconds), tick, value (the keyframed value)
+ - * / %% ^, == != < <= > >=, && || !, a ? b : c
sin cos floor round(x, digits) clamp lerp smoothstep remap min max ...
noise(x, seed) wiggle(freq, amount, seed) rand(seed)
vec(x, y, z) and .x .y .z / .r .g .b .a
Other tracks: Cube.position.y or track("My track").scale; this track: self.position
Shape space: self.local(worldPos), self.world(localPos), also on other shape tracks
Entities: entity("name or UUID").position .velocity .speed .look .health .yaw ... and .nbt (everything it saves, e.g. .nbt.Health), .field (its fields, e.g. .field.hurtTime), .data (synched data, e.g. .data.health)
Full reference: expressions.md
camera.position, camera.yaw, camera.fov
let name = ...; for locals, // for comments, global.name for global variables
vector3.expression.help_text:
Text template: plain text with {expressions} in braces, e.g. Time: {floor(time)} s
{{ and }} are literal braces. {value} is the keyframed text.
format("%%.1f", x), pad(n, 3, "0"), upper, lower, substr, str(x, digits)
vector3.expression.editor.title: Expression editor
vector3.expression.editor.open: Click to edit in the expression editor
vector3.expression.editor.removed: This expression was removed, or its track is gone.
vector3.expression.editor.template_hint: Text template: plain text with {expressions} in braces. A let in one {...} works in the later ones.
vector3.expression.editor.suggestions: Suggestions (Up/Down to choose, Tab or Enter to insert; hover code to see what it holds)
vector3.expression.editor.no_suggestions: Type a name to see matches; after a '.' the members of what is before it are listed.
vector3.expression.editor.globals_hint: Global variables belong to this replay and are read from any expression as global.name. Pick an entity to make a global that refers to it, instead of typing its UUID.
vector3.expression.editor.reference_hint: The full reference is expressions.md in the vector3 repository.
vector3.expression.editor.reference.oper:
Lowest to highest: a ? b : c, ||, &&, == !=, < <= > >=, + -, * / %, unary - + !, ^ (right-associative, binds tighter than unary minus), then .member, [index], .method(), function().
+ joins text when either side is text. % takes the sign of the divisor. Vector arithmetic is per component (a number applies to every component), so a * b is NOT a dot product: use dot(a, b) and cross(a, b).
let name = ...; defines a local; // starts a comment to the end of the line.
vector3.expression.var.value: This parameter's keyframed value, before the expression
vector3.expression.var.self: This track's parameters before its expressions; self.local(p), self.world(p)
vector3.expression.var.camera: The camera: position, yaw, pitch, fov
vector3.expression.fn.mod: remainder with the sign of b
vector3.expression.fn.smoothstep: smooth 0 to 1 between e0 and e1
vector3.expression.fn.remap: map x from one range to another (clamped)
vector3.expression.fn.str: to text, optionally with fixed digits

vector3.expression.fn.uuid: a UUID as text, also from the 4 numbers saved data uses
